body.p: Please enter the Drawing Replacement Sheet, submitted herewith, into the
application. No new matter is included in the Drawing Replacement Sheet.
Claims 1-6, 9-13, 16-19, and 22-24 have been amended. Support for the amendment to

Claim 1 may be found, for example, at page 16, first full paragraph and page 17, first paragraph referring to Fig. 2 in the specification as filed. The amendments to claim 1 incorporate limitations from previously pending Claims 8 and 21, which have been canceled without prejudice or
disclaimer. No new matter is added in the amendments.
The specification has been amended by replacement with the attached substitute

specification. The amendments are described below. Fig. 2 has been amended to add a reference number "51" to the flexible encapsulation layer. No new matter is included in either the amendments to the specification shown in the substitute specification or in the amendments to the
drawings shown in the attached replacement drawing sheet.
Claims 1-7, 9-20, and 22-24 are currently pending in this application. In view of the
amendments and remarks in this response, favorable reconsideration of the present application is
respectfully requested.
The Office Action objected to the drawings because of certain informalities. The Office

Action specifically states that "the "flexible encapsulation layer" as claimed in claims 20-23 must be shown or the feature(s) canceled from the claim(s)." Office Action at page 2. For procedural expediency, Fig. 2 of the present application has been amended to add a reference number "51" to the flexible encapsulation layer in the rolled-up configuration as seen in the replacement sheet submitted herewith. The specification also has been amended to add a reference number "51" to the flexible encapsulation layer as seen in the substitute specification submitted herewith. It is clear from the first full paragraph on page 10 of the specification as filed that the flexible encapsulation is arranged on the first side of the substrate and is arranged radially inward of each of the pressure sensing devices, each of the velocity sensing devices, and/or each of the electrically conductive paths. It is also clear from paragraph spanning pages 11 and 12 of the specification as filed that the encapsulation layer may be formed on top of the patterned layers and the PDMS after step (h). Therefore, adding a reference number "51" to the flexible encapsulation layer in Fig. 2 does not introduce new matter into the application. Withdrawal of the objection is respectfully
requested.
Claims 2, 6, 12-13, 16-19, and 22-23 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly

being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter. The Office Action states that "the phrase "preferably" renders these claims indefinite." Office Action at page 3. For procedural expediency, Claims 2, 6, 12, 13, 16, 18, 19, 22, and 23 have been
amended to delete the term "preferably" as set forth above.
The Office Action also states that "Regarding claim 17, it is unclear what is being claimed

for the phrase "polyamide, PI,". The term "polyamide" appeared as a typographical error in the present application. It is well-known in the art to abbreviate "polyimide" to "PI", and the specification states "polyimide (PI)" on pages 11 and 20." Office Action at page 3. For procedural expediency, Claim 17 has been amended to replace "polyamide, PI," with "polyimide (PI)" as set
forth above. Withdrawal of the rejections is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-5, 10-11, and 16-19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being
unpatentable over U.S. Publication No. 2003/0229388 ("Hayashi" hereinafter) in view of U.S.
Publication No. 2013/0053872 ("Hansen" hereinafter) and "Soft and flexible piezoelectric smart patch for vascular graft monitoring based on Aluminum Nitride thin film" ("Natta" hereinafter).

Claims 6-9, 12-15 and 20-24 were rejected over these same references in view of additional secondary references. Specifically, U.S. Patent No. 9,848,775 ("Tee" hereinafter) was cited in connection with Claims 6-7 and 13, "Regional Differences in the Basal and Maximal Rates of Blood Flow in the Skin" ("Hertzman" hereinafter) was cited in connection with Claim 14, U.S.

Publication No. 2016/0331313 ("Kuraguntla" hereinafter) was cited in connection with Claim 15, WO Publication No. 02/00118 ("Weissman" hereinafter) was cited in connection with Claim 20, "Parylene as a Chronically Stable, Reproducible Microelectrode Insulator" ("Loeb" hereinafter) was cited in connection with Claims 21-23, U.S. Publication No. 2010/0094376 ("Penner"
hereinafter) was cited in connection with Claim 24, and U.S. Publication No. 2010/0181871 ("Daniel" hereinafter) was cited in connection with Claims 8-9 and 12. Daniel was also
additionally cited in rejecting Claim 1.
The Office Action states that the cited references above teach all subject matter described

in the claims as previously pending. Applicant respectfully traverses each rejection, each assertion regarding what the references disclose, and each and every implicit and/or explicit reliance on Official Notice, and Applicant does not acquiesce in the validity of the rejections. To expedite
allowance of this application, however, Applicant has amended independent Claim 1. As discussed
below, Applicant submits that all pending claims are allowable over the cited references.
As noted above, the amendment to claim 1 incorporate limitations from previously pending
Claims 8 and 21. Therefore, the rejection of Claim 1 will be addressed as applied to these previously pending claims, i.e., the Loeb and Daniel references will be considered in connection
with the rejection of Claim 1.
In addition to incorporating the limitations of Claims 8 and 21, Claim 1 has also been

further amended for clarity. Accordingly, as set forth above, Claim 1 now recites, among other things, "a flexible encapsulation layer, which is arranged on the first side of the flexible substrate in the rolled-up configuration such that the flexible encapsulation layer is positioned over said at least one pressure sensing device, said at least one velocity sensing device, and/or an electrically conductive path in the rolled-up configuration." Applicant respectfully submits that, even when combined, the cited references neither teach nor suggest a flexible encapsulation layer arranged on the first side of the flexible substrate and positioned over the pressure sensing device, the velocity sensing device, or the electrically conductive path in the rolled-up configuration in the vascular
graft.
The Office Action at page 15 states the following:

Hayashi fails to disclose wherein the vascular graft further comprises a flexible encapsulation layer .... However, Loeb teaches wherein a vascular graft further comprises a flexible encapsulation layer, which is arranged on the first side of the substrate such that, in the rolled-up configuration, the flexible encapsulation layer is arranged radially inward of each of the pressure sensing devices (Page 3, "All electrodes were coated with a uniform layer of 3-3.5 pm of Parylene-C"), each of the velocity sensing devices, and/or each of the
electrically conductive paths.
Applicant agrees that Hayashi is deficient in its failure to teach or suggest anything regarding the recited flexible encapsulation layer. However, for the reasons set forth below, the Loeb reference
does not address the noted deficiencies in the teachings of Hayashi.
Applicant agrees that Loeb teaches that electrodes are coated with Parylene-C. However,

the electrodes are coated in a deposition chamber for use as extracellular microelectrodes. The extracellular microelectrodes of Loeb are not in a pressure sensing device or velocity sensing device as part of a vascular graft, as recited in pending Claim 1. As stated on pages 122-123 and shown in Fig. 1, Loeb teaches an extracellular microelectrode for recording single-unit action potentials from nervous tissue. Since the extracellular microelectrodes are used to measure the electrical activity (action potentials) of individual neurons, they are placed outside the cells in close proximity to the target neurons to capture the electrical signals generated during neural activity.
These electrodes are commonly positioned in neural tissue, such as brain regions, spinal cord, or
peripheral nerves, where the targeted neurons reside.
In contrast to the coated extracellular microelectrodes of Loeb, the electrodes of the

presently claimed invention are part of a pressure sensing device and a velocity sensing device in a vascular graft. As recited in the claims, the flexible encapsulation layer is positioned over the pressure sensing device, or the velocity sensing device, and/or an electrically conductive path in the rolled-up configuration." The claims further recite that the flexible encapsulation layer is arranged radially inward of the pressure sensing device, the velocity sensing device, and/or the
electrically conductive path.
The advantages of the recited features are described in the specification as filed at page 17,
first paragraph, with reference to Fig. 2, as follows:

The blood flows along the axial direction 31. Since the pressure sensing and velocity sensing devices 5, 7 are arranged along the line, which extends along the axial direction 31, the blood passes each of the devices 5, 7 one after the other. The flexible encapsulation layer 51 is arranged radially inward of each of the pressure sensing devices 5, each of the velocity sensing devices 7, and each of the electrically conductive paths 9, and thereby protects each of the pressure sensing devices 5, each of the velocity sensing devices 7, and
each of the electrically conductive paths 9 from direct contact with blood.
Nothing in the Loeb reference teaches or suggests "a flexible encapsulation layer, which is

arranged on the first side of the flexible substrate in the rolled-up configuration such that the flexible encapsulation layer is positioned over said at least one pressure sensing device, said at least one velocity sensing device, and/or an electrically conductive path in the rolled-up configuration" recited in presently pending Claim 1 or the advantages of these features or protecting the electrically conductive paths from direct contact with blood. Accordingly, the combination of Loeb with Hayashi does not teach or suggest these limitations of pending Claim 1.
The Hansen, Natta or Daniel references cited in the rejections of Claims 8 and 21 do not

address the deficiencies in the combined teachings of Hayashi and Loeb. Hansen describes an occlusion device for preventing blood flow from a blood vessel into an aneurysm; Natta describes a smart patch based on piezoelectric aluminium nitride integrated on the extraluminal surface of a prosthesis, for the continuous monitoring of the vascular graft; and Daniel describes sensors and actuators consisting of a piezo polymer layer 18 shaped as a cantilever. None of these references discloses anything related to the flexible encapsulation layer recited in the claims. Moreover, the other cited secondary references were only cited in connection with recitations of specific dependent claims. Accordingly, even when all the references are combined, they do not lead to a
prima facie showing of obviousness.
In view of the foregoing, Claim 1 is nonobvious and patentable over the cited references.
The remaining rejected claims incorporate all the features of Claim 1 through their dependencies.

Therefore, the dependent claims are also patentable over the prior art for at least the same reasons that Claim 1 is patentable as well as for their own patentable features. For all of the foregoing reasons, withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103, and allowance of the presently
pending claims are respectfully requested.
Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims,

or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any
disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.
Applicant respectfully submits that the claims are in condition for allowance. Furthermore,

any remarks in support of patentability of one claim should not be imputed to any other claim, even if similar terminology is used. Any remarks referring to only a portion of a claim should not be understood to base patentability on that portion; rather, patentability must rest on each claim taken as a whole. Applicant respectfully traverses each of the Examiner's rejections and each of the Examiner's assertions regarding what the prior art shows or teaches, even if not expressly discussed herein. If some issue remains that the Examiner feels can be addressed by an Examiner's
Amendment, the Examiner is cordially invited to call the undersigned for authorization.
Please charge any additional fees, including any fees for additional extension of time, or
credit overpayment to Deposit Account No. 11-1410.
